learning_outcomes.text: Apply advanced linear modeling methods to real data, statistically analyzing their effectiveness.
Understand what dynamic regression models consist of, being able to apply them to data where necessary.
Apply classification techniques to time series analysis.
Know advanced time series models and their connections with other techniques within data science.
Critically analyze the different methods studied for forecasting and apply the most appropriate in each case.
Apply advanced forecasting techniques to real data and generate associated reports.

syllabus_topics: Non-linear relationships. Regression splines. Local linear regression. Logistic regression.
Estimation in dynamic regression models. Regression with ARIMA errors. Forecasts. Stochastic and deterministic trends. Dynamic harmonic regression.
Hierarchical time series. Grouped time series. Bottom-up, top-down, and middle-out approaches. Optimal reconciliation.
Complex seasonality patterns. Autoregressive vectors. Machine learning methods with temporal data.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation in seminars and tutorials (includes online)
Active participation in forums and virtual campus activities
Practical exams (computer lab exercises and assignments)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final grade is the sum of the weighted scores from attendance/participation (5%), virtual campus activities (10%), practical exams (40%), and a final theoretical exam (45%), with no minimum grade requirements for individual components. For the extraordinary July assessment, students will take a written theoretical/practical exam (4.5 points) and a computer-based practical exam (4 points), adding these to their in-course participation grades (sections 1 and 2 from ordinary). For the extraordinary January assessment, students can obtain 100% of the grade from a single theoretical-practical final exam. In all cases, a minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the course.
